channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Rogun Dam project advances with World Bank funding despite past doubts
item.description: Construction on Tajikistan's Rogun Dam project has progressed significantly, with the World Bank approving a $300 million grant, its second round of funding. WeBuild Group began work on Lot 2 and raised the dam's height, increasing reservoir water levels and generation capacity.

item.title: Chinese investors to inject up to $500 million into three wind farms in Akmola region
item.description: Chinese investors have signed agreements to build three wind power stations and modernize an elevator in Kazakhstan's Akmola region. The total investment for these projects could reach $506 million. The wind farms, with a combined capacity of 450 MW, are planned for construction starting in October 2026 and completion by 2028.

item.title: Afghanistan Journalists Center reports increased censorship and pressure on media
item.description: The Afghanistan Journalists Center (AFJC) states that media and journalists face growing restrictions, including pre-publication censorship, protest coverage bans, and pressure for content approval. Restrictions on women journalists have increased, and some international TV broadcasts are banned. The AFJC urges the Taliban to revoke restrictive orders.

item.title: UN allocates over $1.7 million to support women entrepreneurs in Afghanistan
item.description: UN Women will provide $1.7 million to support approximately 1,500 Afghan women entrepreneurs over the next year through a joint initiative with the UNDP. The program includes financial support, business development services, literacy training, and market access assistance, indirectly benefiting over 14,000 people.

item.title: Kazakhstan-China border crossings to close for three days due to PRC National Day
item.description: Vehicle checkpoints on the Kazakhstan-China border will be closed from October 1 to 3 for the People's Republic of China's National Day. The State Revenue Committee of Kazakhstan's Ministry of Finance announced that railway checkpoints will continue to operate normally. Travelers are advised to be aware of these temporary restrictions.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes Making Roads Profitable for Neighboring Countries
item.description: Kazakhstan aims to develop its road and rail networks to generate revenue for neighboring countries as well. Deputy Prime Minister Serik Zhumangarin discussed financing mechanisms with a World Bank representative. The goal is to create a unified Central Asian infrastructure chain, making transit routes profitable for all involved.

item.title: Uzbekistan Strengthens Child Protection Laws, Increasing Liability Measures
item.description: Uzbekistan is taking a significant step to protect children from violence by strengthening liability measures. A draft law addressing this issue is scheduled for review at the lower house's next session on September 29. This initiative aims to enhance child protection mechanisms within the country.

item.title: Uzbekistan plans to enroll 80% of third and fourth-year students in dual education
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to enroll at least 80% of its third and fourth-year university students, approximately 185,000, in dual education programs. This initiative aims to adapt Germany's successful dual education model, where graduates often continue working at their internship companies. The program will prioritize engineering, manufacturing, construction, and agriculture.

item.title: Almaty Unveils Project to Reduce Private Car Use by 20% by 2040
item.description: Almaty plans to reduce private car usage by 20% by 2040, aiming to increase public transport trips to 2.3 million by 2030. The city will develop metro, light rail, and SkyTrain systems, and build logistics hubs. The Kalkaman metro station is set to open by year-end, extending to the "Baryk" hub.

item.title: Labor Rights to Be Monitored During Uzbekistan's Cotton Harvest Season
item.description: Labor rights will be monitored during Uzbekistan's cotton harvest. Parents are urged to create conditions for their children's education and prevent their involvement in cotton picking. This measure aims to ensure fair labor practices and protect children's right to education.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Arrives in Berlin for Talks
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has arrived in Berlin for important negotiations with German leadership. He is also scheduled to visit Munich and meet with executives from leading German companies, financial, and scientific institutions.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev begins official visit to Germany
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has arrived in Germany for an official visit at the invitation of Federal President Frank-Walter Steinmeier. Discussions in Berlin will focus on strengthening strategic partnership between Kazakhstan and Germany. Tokayev will also visit Munich and meet with business leaders and academics.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev arrives in Germany for talks with Steinmeier and Merz
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has arrived in Berlin for an official visit to Germany. He will hold talks with Federal President Frank-Walter Steinmeier and Chancellor Friedrich Merz to discuss strengthening the strategic partnership between Kazakhstan and Germany. Tokayev will also visit Munich and meet with German business and financial leaders.

item.title: Talks and business forums: Tokayev arrives on a visit to Germany
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has arrived in Germany for an official visit at the invitation of Federal President Frank-Walter Steinmeier. In Berlin, Tokayev will hold talks with Steinmeier and Federal Chancellor Friedrich Merz to discuss strengthening the strategic partnership between Kazakhstan and Germany. He will also visit Munich and participate in business forums.

item.title: Kassym-Jomart Tokayev arrives in Germany for an official visit
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has arrived in Germany for an official visit at the invitation of Federal President Frank-Walter Steinmeier. In Berlin, Tokayev is scheduled to hold talks with German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier and Federal Chancellor Friedrich Merz to discuss strengthening the strategic partnership between Kazakhstan and Germany. He will also visit Munich.

item.title: Kazakh Businesses Urge Reversal of Ban on Deductions for Simplified Tax Regime
item.description: Kazakh businesses are again requesting the cancellation of the ban on deductions for transactions with entities under the simplified tax regime. The National Chamber of Entrepreneurs "Atameken" is involved in discussions regarding proposed amendments to the Tax Code.

item.title: Bishkek Vocational Lyceum Graduate Awarded at WorldSkills Shanghai
item.description: Hanifa Syrgakova, a graduate of Vocational Lyceum No. 18 in Bishkek, received the Best of Nation award at the WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 championship. She competed in "Fashion Technology" and achieved the best result among Kyrgyzstan's national team. Kyrgyzstan officially joined the WorldSkills movement in 2023.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Host UN Crime Prevention Congress in 2031
item.description: Uzbekistan will host the 16th UN Congress on Crime Prevention and Criminal Justice in 2031. The decision was announced by Head of the Presidential Administration Saida Mirziyoyeva at the 15th Congress in Abu Dhabi. This signifies international trust in Uzbekistan's openness and readiness for cooperation.

item.title: Tokayev Replaces Defense Minister After Soldiers' Deaths, Orders Army Reform
item.description: Following the deaths of soldiers, Kazakhstan's President Tokayev has replaced the Defense Minister and ordered a reform of the army. Police have contacted individuals who criticized the authorities online after the military personnel's deaths. An earthquake was also felt in Almaty today.

item.title: Flooding in Thailand Causes $320 Million in Economic Damage
item.description: Ongoing heavy rains in Thailand have caused widespread flooding, displacing thousands of people to safer areas. Much of the capital, Bangkok, is submerged, with "floating" market stalls appearing. The floods have resulted in an estimated $320 million in economic damage.

item.title: Child abduction case highlights legal discrepancies between Russia and Kazakhstan
item.description: A mother is seeking the return of her four-year-old son, who has been held by his father for five months. Despite Russian court orders for his arrest and return, the father reportedly ignores Kazakh court decisions. The mother expresses despair over the legal situation and awaits a court hearing.

item.title: Almaty aims to reduce private car trips by 20% by 2040 through public transport expansion
item.description: Almaty plans to decrease private car usage by 20% by 2040 by enhancing public transportation. The city aims to increase public transit trips to 2.3 million by 2030, introducing metro, LRT, and SkyTrain lines. New transport hubs and park-and-ride facilities are also planned.

item.title: Kazakhstan's average per capita income reaches 410,000 tenge in Q2 2026
item.description: Average per capita monetary income in Kazakhstan reached 410,088 tenge in the second quarter of 2026, a 14.0% increase year-on-year, according to the National Statistics Bureau. Per capita household spending averaged 358,584 tenge. Almaty leads in consumer spending with 483,887 tenge.

item.title: Qarmet begins construction of new coke battery No. 8, a significant investment project
item.description: Qarmet has commenced the refractory lining installation for its new coke battery No. 8, marking a major investment. This is the first new coke production capacity built in decades, replacing units from the 1960s. The new batteries will have a capacity of 1.5 million tons of dry coke annually.

item.title: Prosecutor Seeks Four Years Imprisonment for Activist Mavlyan Askarkbekov
item.description: The state prosecutor has requested a four-year prison sentence for activist Mavlyan Askarkbekov from the Leninsky District Court of Bishkek. The specific charges or details of the case were not provided in the source text.

item.title: Uzbek Grandmaster Javohir Sindarov Named Best Male Chess Player by FIDE
item.description: Uzbekistan's Javohir Sindarov won the Best Chess Player — Male award at the inaugural FIDE Excellence Awards 2026. The ceremony took place during the 46th World Chess Olympiad in Samarkand.

item.title: Almaty Court Demands Increased Anti-Corruption Measures in Police After Fatal Accident
item.description: Following a fatal traffic accident on Al-Farabi Avenue, an Almaty court has issued a private ruling demanding enhanced anti-corruption measures within the city's police department. The ruling came after a former deputy police chief's driver was convicted for dereliction of duty related to the accident, which resulted in three deaths.

item.title: Kazakhstan Increases Milk Exports, Primarily to Russia and Uzbekistan
item.description: Kazakhstan's milk production increased by 0.2% in the first eight months of the year compared to 2025, reaching 441.3 thousand tons. Milk exports rose by 3.0% to 2.9 thousand tons in January-July, with Russia, Uzbekistan, and Tajikistan being the main destinations, according to state media.

item.title: Dollar Exchange Rate Decreases Again in Uzbekistan
item.description: The Central Bank of Uzbekistan announced the exchange rates for foreign currencies against the Uzbek soum, effective September 29. The dollar exchange rate has seen a further decrease.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Fruit and Vegetable Exports to Latvia Reach 7 Million Euros
item.description: Uzbekistan's exports of fruit and vegetable products to Latvia have reached 7 million euros. A project, supported by the Latvian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, aims to develop safe food production and export. Uzbek specialists improved their qualifications in Latvia regarding phytosanitary export systems and food safety.

item.title: HIV/AIDS Prevention Campaign Conducted for Bus Drivers in Tashkent
item.description: An awareness campaign and free screening for HIV/AIDS was held for drivers and staff at a bus depot in Tashkent's Mirzo Ulugbek district. Specialists informed participants about transmission routes, risk factors, and prevention measures. Voluntary blood samples were collected for free screening. Such events aim to increase medical literacy and early disease prevention among workforces.

item.title: Kazakhstan Postpones Construction of Almaty-Issyk-Kul Highway Project
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Transport has postponed the Almaty-Issyk-Kul highway project, citing lower priority in the current planning phase. State resources are focused on other infrastructure projects crucial for socio-economic development. The project's implementation may be reconsidered in future planning cycles.

item.title: 14 Kazakh Servicemen Die During Caspian Sea Military Exercises
item.description: Fourteen Kazakh servicemen died during the "Khazar Qorgany – 2026" military exercises in the Caspian Sea. The incident occurred during a landing operation when a large wave hit the unit. The Ministry of Defense cited adverse weather conditions, prompting an investigation and the dismissal of the defense minister.

item.title: UN Report: 21 Million Adolescent Girls Become Mothers Annually in Developing Countries
item.description: The UN Human Rights Office reports that 12.3 million girls aged 10-19 became mothers in 2025, often unprepared. Poverty, race, education, location, and conflict exacerbate risks. Preventable maternal mortality is higher for adolescent mothers, and many lack access to contraception.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Implement Automated System for Issuing Certificates of Conformity
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet of Ministers is introducing an automated system for issuing certificates of conformity. Government agencies are developing the platform and integrating information systems for electronic document processing and issuance, as reported by the Cabinet's press service.

item.title: Tajikistan participates in CIS Council meeting on economic security
item.description: An official delegation from Tajikistan's Agency for State Financial Control and Anti-Corruption attended the 25th meeting of the CIS Coordination Council of Tax Investigation Bodies in Tashkent on September 23, 2026. Participants discussed economic security, combating financial crimes, and countering transnational crime.

item.title: Tajikistan's Foreign Minister Addresses UN General Assembly on Peace and Water
item.description: Tajikistan's Foreign Minister Sirojiddin Mukhriddin spoke at the UN General Assembly, emphasizing peace, multilateral cooperation, and the UN's central role. He announced Tajikistan's initiative for a "Decade of Peace" (2027-2036) and highlighted the upcoming UN Water Conference in Dushanbe in 2028.

item.title: Bishkek court reclassifies charges in '75 Letters' case, lawyer explains
item.description: Lawyers for the accused in Bishkek's "75 Letters" case have received the full court ruling. The charges were reclassified from "obstruction of citizens' electoral rights" under Article 326 to Article 195. This reclassification avoids a prison sentence, as Article 326 is considered a particularly serious crime. The Supreme Court may further reduce the sentence.

item.title: South Korean President's Office Demands Apology from Ukraine
item.description: The South Korean president's office has demanded an apology from Ukraine. This demand stems from reports that North Korean prisoners of war were handed over to Seoul, causing a dispute between the two nations.

item.title: Pakistan Rejects Taliban Claims of Involvement in Afghan Border Clashes
item.description: Pakistan's Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has denied Taliban allegations of Pakistani involvement in clashes in Afghanistan's Nuristan and Kunar provinces. The ministry called the claims baseless and described circulating videos as false narratives intended to portray domestic opposition as foreign-backed.
